idiom_name: companion-object smart constructors over sealed abstract case class private; require as backstop
implementation_notes: Scala absorbs the two-class Essence/CreationTarget structure into the language itself: the companion object takes the Essence role, its smart-constructor factory validates the compulsory properties and returns Option[Contract] or Either[ValidationError, Contract], so an instance that fails validation is simply never produced - a missing or invalid compulsory property becomes a None/Left value instead of a half-valid object. The CreationTarget half is a case class with val constructor parameters (immutable compulsory properties) whose access is fenced by the compiler: `sealed abstract case class Contract private (...)` suppresses the synthesized apply and copy bypasses, blocks `new` and anonymous subclassing outside the file, and leaves the factory as the only path - the classic restricted-constructor requirement, enforced by access modifiers instead of friend declarations. Predef require in the class body is the documented design-by-contract backstop that blames the caller with IllegalArgumentException on every construction path (the analogue of Essence.validateParameters() early feedback is Try(Contract(...)) or the factory's Left branch; cats ValidatedNec with mapN accumulates all violated rules at once). The classic form is still justified only when validation must be interactive and stateful across many fields (a form-like wizard) or when the Essence must be reused to stamp out multiple targets with shared values - otherwise named/default parameters plus the factory make a separate Essence class redundant.
pitfalls: `case class Email private (value: String)` alone does NOT close the gate: the compiler still synthesizes a public `apply` on the companion and a public `copy`, so `Email("bad")` and `good.copy(value = "bad")` both mint unvalidated instances. Since 2.12.2 (and via -Xsource:3 on 2.13.2+) a private constructor propagates to the synthesized copy/apply, but the version-independent fence is `sealed abstract case class ... private`, where apply/copy are never generated and `new Email(v) {}` is only possible inside the file (sealed).

Predef require/check are no security boundary: they are elidable (scalac -Xelide-below above ASSERTION, -Xdisable-assertions) and merely throw - an elided `require` lets an invalid instance escape silently. Keep the type-level gate (private constructor + smart constructor) as the enforcement and treat require as a development-time backstop; prefer require (IllegalArgumentException, blames the caller) over check (IllegalStateException) at construction so failure semantics stay honest.

Exception-driven validation (require in the constructor) is the non-idiomatic face of the pattern in Scala: the functional form returns the failure as a value (Either[ValidationError, T], cats ValidatedNec accumulated with mapN), which also gives the  Essence.validateParameters() early-feedback behaviour for free - callers can inspect the Left before any domain object exists.

The generic Essence<->CreationTarget circular-dependency trap dissolves only if the factory stays in the companion object: companions share private access by language rule. Move the smart constructor to a separate file or object and the private constructor becomes unreachable (or temptingly widened to public), reopening the bypassing-Essence hole.

val fields are shallow-immutable: a compulsory property typed as a mutable collection (scala.collection.mutable.Seq) or an array can be corrupted after validation, so the always-valid invariant checked at creation silently breaks; use List/Vector, and prefer immutable case-class state anyway because unstable equals/hashCode corrupts the dictionary-key/database-index use cases the pattern targets.
